newsitem.title: USA: Alliance may open drug trial to children.
newsitem.headline: Alliance may open drug trial to children.

text.p: Alliance Pharmaceutical Corp said Tuesday it was considering including pediatric patients in a Phase II/III adult trial of LiquiVent planned for late 1997.

In April, due to an unexpected substantial decrease in the mortality rate of the control group, Alliance suspended a Phase III pediatric trial in which it had enrolled almost 200 patients for treatment of Acute Respitory Distress Syndrome (ARDS).
Historically the mortality rate of pediatric ARDS patients is over 30 percent, but only about 10 percent of the controls died in the study.
Alliance CEO Duane Roth said at the Cruttenden Roth Healthcare Conference here that his company was eager to resume pediatric trials.
He said it was considering "incorporating children into the adult study that we hope to start between September and December."
Alliance said last month that the Phase II/III trial of adult ARDS patients would be delayed about six months, until autumn, in the wake of the pediatric trial so it could review the trial designs.
Roth said the company was also considering designing a new Phase III study limited to pediatric patients.
He said Alliance was still analyzing the data from the suspended pediatric trial.
LiquiVent, being co-developed with Hoechst Marion Rousell, has FDA "fast track" status. It is an oxygen-carrying liquid administered directly to the lungs for treatment of acute respitory failure.
The company aims to bring it to market by 1999 with hopes of a $1 billion market.
